title: AccessGrantLogRow
description: One ledger-service access_grant_log row as the grant-log exporter writes it to the write-once audit store, at access-grant-log/<database_generation>/<chain_seq, 20 digits>.json. The object is the RFC 8785 bytes of canonical_v2, which refuses JSON numbers, so every integer is a decimal string. The root $schema keyword names the JSON Schema dialect; the payload property $schema names this schema.

$schema.description: Published URL of the frozen schema version that describes this row object. A stored object keeps it for its whole retention, so it never names the latest URL, which a later version replaces.

create_time.description: Insert time under the chain lock, cut to the millisecond

create_submillisecond_micros.description: Microseconds within the millisecond of create_time, 0 to 999. The row hash takes the insert time as the Unix milliseconds of create_time * 1000 + create_submillisecond_micros microseconds.

before.description: Version 2: the document its canonical bytes hold. Version 1: PostgreSQL's jsonb::text rendering, which the version 1 hash covers.

else.description: Version 2, the rules the verifier checks before an upload: a site_id is at least 1, actor_issuer_id and revision are not negative, change_type, actor_subject and alert are not empty, each document and its canonical bytes are both set or both null, a document holds no JSON number (canonical_v2 refuses them), the revision is set, and an approver is absent or a principal: an issuer ID of at least 1 and a subject with a character outside Python's str.isspace set, the test the verifier applies (the character class of ck_access_grant_log_reason, so every regex engine agrees). Version 1 rows get only what the database holds (signed integers, empty strings, a canonical value), because the verifier checks their columns not at all.

timestamp.description: Instant as an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp with Z and exactly 3 fraction digits (milliseconds), the form of common/v2.0.0 $defs/timestamp

signedDecimal.description: A signed integer column the database does not constrain; version 1 rows may hold any value

canonicalHex.description: The canonical bytes of a version 2 document as hex; the shortest document, {}, is 2 bytes
